name: Systemia Portfolio Sentinel
problem: Organizations with growing software estates lose track of which apps, repositories, workflows, public endpoints and machine-discovery surfaces are actually healthy. Systemia Portfolio Sentinel continuously inventories known surfaces, detects material drift, deduplicates repeat failures and routes evidence-backed repair work without exposing private topology.
intent_terms: monitor my software portfolio for broken products
continuously audit all of our apps repositories and public URLs
tell me when one of our software products breaks
detect broken deployments and stale workflows
watch GitHub Actions and public product doors for failures
find drift across our apps APIs workflows and discovery surfaces
open repair work automatically when software breaks
our company has too many apps and we do not know what is broken
keep an inventory of all our software and verify it stays healthy
monitor LLM discovery pages and agent endpoints
detect product URL workflow and deployment regressions
pricing: Commercial pilot is custom-quoted based on portfolio size, repositories, public endpoints, workflow count and monitoring scope. No fixed public price or direct machine checkout is currently advertised.
confirmation: Public discovery is read-only. Monitoring private repositories, internal systems or customer infrastructure requires explicit scoped authorization. Production changes, payment actions and external communications remain separately gated.
payment_authority: No direct machine checkout is exposed. Commercial terms and any later payment require explicit human agreement and authoritative payment verification.
invocation_status: LIVE for public machine discovery, deterministic problem matching, read-only pilot handoff, and human-confirmed commercial pilot request capture through Evercraft Machine Commerce. The internal Portfolio Sentinel runtime now has receipt-backed commerce-integrity cycle code for product-native buyer-route reachability, gateway-leak detection and conversion-stage telemetry. Recurring cadence is not claimed until an authorized scheduler is configured and successive runtime receipts prove it. Customer monitoring begins only after separate scoped onboarding and authorization. A pilot request grants no private access, monitoring authority, payment obligation, production mutation, or external-system authority.
